title: Queensland electronic billboards visible from state-controlled roads
source_title: Roadside Advertising Manual, Edition 4, Technical Volume (Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads, December 2022)
status_note: Every value checked against the Technical Volume on 22 October 2026 (section and page citations below), downloaded from the source URL; not yet independently reviewed

citations.creative.motion.allowed: s. 3.6, p. 19 (non-static electronic displays not permitted to be visible to drivers); s. 3.6.1.2 and 3.6.1.3, p. 20
citations.creative.motion.no_flashing: s. 3.6.1.3, p. 20 ("not permitted to move, flash or change brightness")
citations.creative.no_traffic_device_imagery: s. 2.1, p. 3 (imitates a traffic control device; gives instructions to traffic); s. 2.1.1, pp. 4-5 (shape and colour)
citations.creative.no_sequencing: s. 3.6.1.3, p. 20 (sequential or multi-frame messages, on one billboard or successive billboards)
citations.playback.failure_state: s. 3.6.1.3, p. 20 ("default to" a blank screen)

notes: Page numbers are the Technical Volume's printed page numbers. Section 3.6 applies to electronic billboards on private property or within state-controlled roads that are visible from a state-controlled road, motorway or motorway-standard road; electronic billboards of 4 m² or less follow the same operating rules (s. 4.4, p. 30). Roads controlled by local government are outside the manual.

Edition 4 was still the current edition on the department's manual page as captured by web.archive.org in May 2026 (Edition 3 is listed as replaced in December 2022). The department's own page refuses automated requests, so the amendment register wasn't read.

Dwell: Table 3.6.1.4 gives 10 s for a state-controlled road with a speed limit 'less than and not equal to 80 km/h', 15 s at 80 km/h and above, and 25 s for any device visible from a motorway or motorway-standard road. Placement can't say whether a road is a motorway, so the 25 s rule is a note on every band; a publisher with such a screen should set rules.playback.min_dwell_s to 25.

Transition: the source requires less than 0.5 s, with no 'fly in', 'scroll' or other change effects and no blank screen between messages. max_transition_s is an upper bound, so 0.5 s is the closest value.
failure_state is 'blank': the source requires a blank screen on any malfunction, and doesn't say what colour.

Not encoded: luminance. For electronic billboards Table 3.6.1.5 (p. 21) sets maximums by the ambient light measured at the sign (150 cd/m² at 0-10 lux, 200 at 11-40, 250 at 41-100, 400 at 101-400, 700 at 401-1,000, 1,500 at 1,001-4,000, 2,300 at 4,001-10,000, 4,000 at 10,001-40,000 and 6,000 at 40,001-100,000 lux), which no lighting period or zone can select. Section 3.6 takes precedence over the general limits of Appendix D, Table D1 (p. 135: 500, 350 and 300 cd/m² in lighting environment zones 1-3), which apply to other illuminated devices.
Not encoded: legibility. Section 2.1.1 (pp. 6-7) gives capital letter heights for 6, 9 and 12-word signs but says they are advisory, not mandatory.

Not encoded: no split screens (s. 3.6.1.3), data logging (s. 3.6.1.7), spacing, advance visibility of at least 3 s and other siting criteria (s. 3.6.2), which aren't creative or playback rules. The department's factsheet on small electronic devices in school zones wasn't read.

Discrepancies with the OMA Digital Signage Policy (February 2024, Table 1), which this pack replaces as the Queensland pack: the OMA says 15 s 'above 80 km/h', where the manual says 80 km/h and above, and it lists 25 s as a speed band where the manual ties it to visibility from a motorway. The OMA treats motion as an industry position, but the manual doesn't permit non-static displays visible to drivers.
